title: Lumpia Wrappers (Spring Roll Wrappers)
description: Lumpia wrappers are also referred to as Popiah and more generally as spring roll wrappers are thin paper-like skins. They are soft and light textured but they are strong enough to wrap and hold your fillings without breaking apart.

steps.text: Gradually add the water while mixing simultaneously until a soft and viscous batter is formed, now work the batter by lifting it and slamming it on the bowl

steps.text: Cover it up and leave it to rest in the fridge until it's really cold or better still leave it overnight.

steps.text: The next day the Batter would have hardened up. Now work it a little bit just to be able to hold it in the cup of your hand - Please refer to the video.

steps.text: Now preheat your pan on a medium to low heat for about 2 to 4 minutes (the amount of time for heating your pan is dependent on the thickness of your pan) and smear the dough in a fast circular motion on the heated pan.

raw.text: Now preheat your pan on a medium to low heat for about 2 to 4 minutes (the amount of time for heating your pan is dependent on the thickness of your pan) and smear the dough in a fast circular motion on the heated pan.

steps.text: After a couple of seconds, the edge of the wrap will start to curl up, carefully lift the wrap by the curled edge to lift the wrap off the pan.

steps.text: Place the wraps in a bowl and cover it with a damp towel to prevent it from drying up.

steps.text: You can store the wraps in a plastic bag and store in the fridge for a couple of days or freeze for a couple of months. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: Hi Lola! Thanks for the video! My parents used to make their own lumpia wrappers when I was growing up, exactly like this! There were no Filipino stores where they could purchase them at that time. It brought back great memories to watch your video. I’m inspired to try it myself!

Just wanted to share, what a great video.  Simple, clear concise and with such a beautiful accent narrating the whole adventure.  Thank you for taking the time to educate us with not only your passion but your kindness in teaching as well.  
I can't wait to try and make these at home myself.
